title: Enterprise region eligibility and failover scaling triage guidance
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a pragmatic triage playbook for enterprise customer requests that require new region availability or special data residency/failover constraints. The goal is to standardize the initial qualification, risk/cost estimate, and handback to sales/solutions engineering with clear next steps and SLAs. This doc captures acceptance criteria, decision matrix, required artifacts, staging path, and a minimal orchestration checklist for quick yes/no outcomes.
background: We receive varied enterprise requests: new region provisioning, strict data residency (no egress from a jurisdiction), and contractual failover guarantees (e.g., multi-region active/passive within X minutes). Current intake is ad hoc across Solutions, Sales, and Customer Success which slows sales cycles and causes mismatched expectations. This playbook aims to reduce time-to-decision and ensure consistent downstream engineering and legal scope.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form version published and accessible to Sales & CS (Confluence link)
Triage rubric that returns: Eligible / Needs Engineering Scope / Requires Legal Exception
Estimated cost band (low/medium/high) and minimal implementation timeline provided within 3 business days
Clear handback artifacts: recommended rollout path, infra dependencies, security review flag, and template SOW language
Runbook for controlled failover testing (staging playbook) included
triage_steps: 1) Intake: Capture product, data residency requirement, RTO/RPO expectations, contract language, customer priority, and billing model
2) Quick eligibility check (Product): Is model supported in existing infra variants? Any legal/regulatory hard blocks?
3) Failure-mode mapping: Map requested failover behavior to existing routing policies and fallback tiers
4) Cost bucket estimate: Map to predefined cost bands and reserved capacity implications
5) Risk and dependency list: Identify infra blockers (capacity, network peering, KMS), and compliance needs (audit logs, data residency proof)
6) Output: Triage decision + artifact bundle for Solutions/Sales (incl. template SOW if approved)
decision_matrix: A: Eligible - low effort: region already provisionable, no residency egress, fallbacks supported. Next: Sales handback with pricing delta.
B: Scoped-Engineering - requires infra config or modest provisioning (2-8 weeks). Next: Engineering intake + prioritized ticket with estimate.
C: Legal/Policy - requires contractual/insurance exceptions or on-prem solution. Next: Legal review + enterprise archetype engagement.
D: Deferred - strategic/regulatory constraints or very high cost. Next: Document scope and propose alternative (fallback region + data partitioning)
required_artifacts_on_handback: Customer contract excerpts with residency clauses
Desired RTO/RPO and traffic profile (TPS, concurrency, sequence length distribution)
Data classification and KMS region requirements
Customer acceptance criteria and go/no-go metrics for failover testing
infrastructure_dependencies: Cross-region networking / VPC peering maturity in target cloud region
Dedicated vs shared capacity implications (must flag Dedicated requirement)
KMS/HSM keys in target region or supported cross-region encryption policy
Observability hooks: tracing, per-route cost metrics, and SLO dashboards must be enabled for the rollout
cost_estimation_guidance: Low: configuration-only changes, uses existing pooled capacity. Expected delta < 10% ARR impact.
Medium: requires reserved capacity or small GPU pool provisioning. Expected delta 10%-50% of baseline run rate.
High: new data center footprint, on-prem or air-gapped deployment. Expected delta >50% and likely requires contract amendment
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Speed vs. Compliance — quick region provisioning using hosted infra may not satisfy contractual residency; slower Dedicated/Private route meets residency but increases cost and time.
Tradeoff: Predictable SLA vs. Unit Cost — offering hard multi-region failover with tight RTO often requires reserved capacity or hot-standby which raises unit cost for the customer.
Recommendation: Prefer templated SOWs and a small matrix of supported region/residency archetypes to avoid ad-hoc engineering exceptions.
If a customer requires immutable residency guarantees (no outbound egress), propose Redwood Private deployment as default; document escalation path and expected timeline.
